p.src: The story tells how Yang Zhi had been robbed of the Birthday Gifts on Yellow Mud Ridge. How could he return and face Grand Secretary Liang? He was ready to seek death there on the ridge. Just as he was about to fling himself down from Yellow Mud Ridge, he suddenly came to his senses and checked his step. He thought, “My parents brought me into this world, a fine, imposing man, and from childhood I mastered all eighteen kinds of martial skill. Surely my life cannot end like this.... Rather than seek a place to die today, I had better wait until they catch me someday and settle the matter then.” When he turned and looked again at the fourteen men, they could only stare wide-eyed at Yang Zhi; not one of them could struggle to his feet. Pointing at them, Yang Zhi cursed, “All this happened because you scoundrels would not heed me, and now you have dragged me down with you!” He picked up his staff-sword from beside a tree root, hung his saber at his waist, and looked all around. Seeing nothing else, Yang Zhi sighed and went straight down the ridge.

p.src: Not until the second watch did the fourteen men finally awaken. One after another they crawled to their feet, crying out an unbroken stream of complaints. The old superintendent said, “None of you would listen to Commander Yang’s sound advice, and today you have ruined me too!” The men said, “Sir, what is done is done. Let us first put our heads together.” The old superintendent said, “What ideas could you possibly have?” They said, “We were in the wrong. But the ancients said, ‘When fire reaches your own body, each man must brush it off himself; when a hornet crawls into your robe, strip it off at once.’ If Commander Yang were still here, none of us could talk our way out of it. But now he has gone off to parts unknown. When we return to face His Excellency Grand Secretary Liang, why not lay all the blame on him? We need only say, ‘All along the road he abused and beat us, intimidating us so thoroughly that we could do nothing. He was in league with the brigands. He drugged us senseless, bound our hands and feet, and carried off all the gold and treasure.’” The old superintendent said, “That story will serve. At daybreak we shall first report the crime to the local authorities. We shall leave the two officers here to attend the court and await orders while the thieves are pursued and arrested. The rest of us will hurry through the night back to Beijing and report the matter to our lord. He can issue official dispatches, inform the Grand Tutor, and charge Jizhou Prefecture with hunting down this band of robbers. That will settle it.” At dawn the next day, the old superintendent and his party went to lodge their complaint with the responsible officials of Jizhou Prefecture. Of that there is no more to tell.

Looking behind, he saw the young wine-server coming after them with a pronged rake, leading another two or three farmhands, each carrying a staff. All came racing toward him as though on wings. p.src: Yang Zhi and Cao Zheng kept Lu Zhishen under close guard and escorted him up the mountain. When they saw the three passes, they found them truly forbidding: mountains curved around from both sides and enclosed the temple. The peaks rose in majestic strength, with only a single road leading up through the passes. At each of the three successive passes stood rolling logs and stones, stout crossbows and powerful bows, while bitter-bamboo spears bristled densely together. After passing the three barred gates, they came before Baozhu Temple. There they saw three temple gates and a stretch of ground as level as a mirror, all enclosed by a wooden stockade like a fortress wall. Seven or eight underlings stood beneath the temple's front gate. Seeing Lu Zhishen brought in bound, they all pointed at him and cursed, “You bald donkey! You wounded our chief, but today you've been caught at last! We'll take our time slicing this wretch to pieces!” Lu Zhishen said nothing. Deng Long said, “You bald donkey! The other day you knocked me down and injured my belly; the dark swelling has yet to subside. Now the day has come when you must face me again.” Lu Zhishen opened his fierce eyes wide and roared, “Don't run, you bastard!” The two farmhands gave the ends of the rope a single tug, undoing the slipknots and loosening the bonds. Lu Zhishen took his monk's staff from Cao Zheng and whirled it like flying clouds. Yang Zhi flung off his broad hat and raised the long-handled saber in his hand. Cao Zheng also brandished his staff. All the farmhands sprang into action together and pressed forward with united strength. Before Deng Long could struggle to his feet, Lu Zhishen's monk's staff came down squarely on his head, splitting his skull in two and smashing the chair beneath him as well. Yang Zhi had already stabbed down four or five of the underlings. Cao Zheng shouted, “Come and surrender, all of you! Anyone who refuses will be swept away and put to death!” The five or six hundred underlings and several junior leaders throughout the temple were stunned senseless with terror and had no choice but to come forward and submit. They immediately ordered Deng Long's corpse and the other bodies carried to the rear mountain and burned. At the same time, they had the granaries inventoried and the lodgings put in order, then went to inspect how much property lay behind the temple. For the moment, they had wine and meat prepared for a meal. Lu Zhishen and Yang Zhi became the stronghold's chiefs and held a feast of wine in celebration. All the underlings submitted, and junior leaders were again appointed to command them.

Yang Zhi and the seven bandits loaded all the treasure from the Birthday Gifts, together with our baggage, onto the carts and carried it away. The rest of us traveled through the night to hurry back and inform Your Excellency.”

p.src: Now He Tao, having received the command, left the hall and went to the constables’ quarters. He gathered the many officers together in the confidential chamber to discuss the case. The officers merely looked at one another, as mute as geese whose beaks were pierced by arrows or fish whose cheeks were caught on hooks; not one of them spoke. He Tao said, “Ordinarily you all sit in this room earning money to spend, but now that a difficult and urgent case has arisen, none of you says a word. At least take pity on the words tattooed upon my face.” They replied, “With respect, Inspector, we are men, not grass or trees. How could we fail to understand? But those men posing as merchants must have been outlaws from deep mountains and empty wastes in some distant prefecture. They happened upon the convoy, robbed its treasure, and returned to their stronghold to enjoy themselves. How could they possibly be caught? p.src: His wife saw him and asked, “Husband, why do you look like this today?” He Tao said, “You do not know. The other day the prefect assigned me an official warrant concerning a band of robbers on Yellow Mud Ridge. They stole eleven loads of gold, pearls, and other treasures that Secretariat Liang was sending to his father-in-law, Grand Tutor Cai, in celebration of his birthday. No one knows what sort of men took them. Since receiving that honored order, I have yet to apprehend anyone. Today I went to request an extension, only to find that the Grand Tutor’s residence had sent another administrator, who was waiting there and demanding that this band be captured and escorted to the capital. p.src: While they were speaking, He Tao’s younger brother He Qing came to visit him. He Tao said, “What have you come for? Why are you here instead of out gambling?” He Tao’s quick-witted wife hurriedly beckoned to him and said, “Brother-in-law, come into the kitchen a moment. I have something to tell you.” He Qing followed his sister-in-law into the kitchen and sat down. His sister-in-law prepared some wine, meat, and vegetables, warmed several cups of wine, and invited He Qing to drink. He Qing asked his sister-in-law, “My brother treats people far too cruelly! Worthless though I may be, I am still his own brother! However grand he may be, he is only a police inspector. Would it disgrace him so much to invite me to share a cup of wine?” His sister-in-law said, “Brother-in-law, you do not understand. Your brother is so troubled he can scarcely go on living!” He Qing said, “What happened to all the money and goods he takes in every day? He has plenty of money and rice. What could make life impossible for him?” His sister-in-law said, “You do not know. The other day, on Yellow Mud Ridge, a band of travelers posing as date merchants robbed the Birthday Convoy that Secretariat Liang of the Northern Capital was sending in celebration of Grand Tutor Cai’s birthday. Now the prefect of Jizhou has received the Grand Tutor’s strict command that every bandit must be captured within ten days and escorted to the capital. If the actual culprits cannot be caught, your brother will be tattooed and exiled to some remote and pestilent military prefecture. Did you not see that the prefect has already had the words ‘Repeatedly exiled to ... Prefecture’ tattooed on your brother’s face? Only the destination remains unfilled. If he fails to catch them soon, he truly will suffer! How could he be in any mood to drink with you? That is why I just prepared some wine and food for you myself. He has been brooding for some time, so you must not blame him.”

p.src: He Qing said, “I too vaguely heard people saying, ‘Some bandits robbed the Birthday Convoy.’ Where exactly did it happen?” His sister-in-law said, “I only heard that it was on Yellow Mud Ridge.” He Qing asked, “And what sort of people robbed it?” His sister-in-law said, “Brother-in-law, you are not drunk. I just told you: seven travelers posing as date merchants robbed it.” He Qing laughed aloud. “So that is how it was. If you know they were date merchants, why be so distressed? Why not send some sharp men to arrest them?” His sister-in-law said, “That is easily said, but there is nowhere to begin searching.” He Qing laughed. “Sister-in-law, you need not worry. My brother keeps a regular company of fine wine-and-meat friends while ordinarily ignoring his own brother. Now that trouble has come, he claims there is nowhere to catch the culprits. If only his brother were allowed to learn the truth and earn a few strings of cash to spend, what difficulty could this pack of petty thieves present?” His sister-in-law asked, “Brother-in-law, can it be that you know some clue?” He Qing laughed. “Just wait until my brother is in mortal danger. Then his younger brother will come forward with a way to save him.” With that, he rose to leave. His sister-in-law detained him and made him drink two more cups.

p.src: The woman found these words suspicious and hurried to tell her husband everything in detail. He Tao at once had his brother summoned before him. He Tao put on a conciliatory smile and said, “Brother, if you know where these bandits have gone, why will you not save me?” He Qing said, “I know nothing of their origins. I was only joking with my sister-in-law. How could your little brother possibly save you?” He Tao said, “My good brother, do not stand aside and watch whether I fare well or ill. Think only of how well I have treated you in ordinary times, forget the wrongs I did you in idle moments, and save my life!” He Qing said, “Brother, you command so many sharp-eyed and nimble constables—two or three hundred of them. Why do you not have them exert themselves for you? What can one man like me do to save you?” He Tao said, “Brother, say no more of them. There seems to be a lead in what you say; do not give someone else the chance to play the hero. Just tell me something of their whereabouts, and I will see that you are well rewarded. Only then can you set my mind at ease!” He Qing said, “What whereabouts could there be? I know nothing about it!” He Tao said, “Do not torment me. Remember that we were born of the same mother.” He Qing said, “Do not panic. Wait until matters become truly desperate; then I shall come and lend my strength to seize this band of petty thieves.” His sister-in-law then said, “Brother-in-law, do whatever you can to save your brother; that too is the duty of kin. The Grand Preceptor’s office has now issued an urgent warrant demanding these people at once. This is an affair as vast as heaven, yet you call them petty thieves!” He Qing said, “Sister-in-law, you ought to know how much abuse I have endured from my brother merely over my gambling. Yet however he beat or cursed me, I never once quarreled with him. Ordinarily, whenever there is wine and food, he enjoys them with others; but today his brother can be of some use to him.”

p.src: Seeing that there was indeed some substance behind his words, He Tao hurriedly took out a ten-tael ingot of silver, set it on the table, and said, “Brother, accept this ingot for the time being. When the bandits are caught and the gold, silver, and bolts of silk are awarded, I shall personally see to your full reward.” He Qing laughed and said, “Brother, this is truly ‘clutching at the Buddha’s feet in a crisis, though you burn no incense in peaceful times.’ If I were to take your silver, it would be as though I were extorting you. Put it away for now; do not use it to ensnare me later. If you persist in this, I shall say nothing. Since you and your wife have both spoken kindly to me, I will tell you. Do not bring out silver to frighten me.” He Tao said, “The silver all comes from the authorities’ promised reward. How could there not be three or five hundred strings of cash? Brother, do not refuse it. Let me first ask you this: what lead do you have concerning these bandits?” He Qing slapped his thigh and said, “I have this whole band of thieves right here in my pouch.” He Tao exclaimed in astonishment, “Brother, how can you say that these bandits are in your pouch?” He Qing said, “Brother, never mind how; suffice it to say that I have them here. Just put away the silver. Do not use it to entrap me later; treat me only as kin should. Then I shall tell you all about it.”
